# Contributing

For an AI agent or a person changing this repo. Read it before your first edit.

## Why this file exists

This repo is a standalone checkout that installs into each tool's home folder. The root `AGENTS.md` (imported by root `CLAUDE.md`) holds short contributor rules only, while the product rulebook lives in `core/AGENTS.md` (and the Antigravity rulebook built from it must stay under a 24,000-byte cap). Detailed contributor notes live here so neither `core/AGENTS.md` nor root `AGENTS.md` grows large.

## Sources and generated files

Edit the sources. Never hand-edit a generated file; regenerate it.

| Sources (edit these) | What they are |
|---|---|
| `core/AGENTS.md` | The tool-neutral product rulebook |
| `core/roles/*.md` | The agent roles: the five core roles and the six review-panel roles (`review-*`) |
| `adapters/<tool>.mjs` + `adapters/<tool>.notes.md` | One adapter per tool, and its tool notes |
| `models.json` | Tier to model, per tool |
| `profiles/*.md` | Optional rulebook additions |
| `standards/*.md` | The coding-standards archive, one file per stack (format in `standards/README.md`) |
| `review/` | The review panel: procedure, explorer contract, lane checklists, calibration, regression corpus and metrics formats |
| `workflows/*.md`, `templates/` | The portable workflows (`/start`, `/draft-pr` and others) and the target-repo rulebook template |
| `orchestration/standards.md`, `orchestration/sprint.md`, `orchestration/board.md`, `orchestration/brief.md`, `orchestration/wrap-up.md` | The tool-neutral routine procedures: the standards setup, sprint mode, board writes, marching orders and the finish |
| `orchestration/sprint/` | Sprint assets read from the setup checkout: `story-template.html`, its filler `make-story.mjs`, and `theme/` |
| `core/procedures.mjs` | The procedure catalogue: each routine, workflow and review procedure with its source file; the Claude Code and Antigravity adapters render thin wrapper skills and commands from it. To add a procedure, write its neutral file, add an entry, give each of those adapters its notes for it (`procedureNotes`), then run `golden` |
| `.claude/skills/ship-prompts/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/ship-prompts/SKILL.md` | Project skill for developing this repo, shipped identically for Claude Code and Antigravity (loaded only in a session opened here; other files under `.claude/` and `.agents/` stay untracked) |
| `adapters/claude-code/` | Claude-only static assets: `skills/orc-permissions/SKILL.md` (installed by `install --tool claude-code` and `sync` beside the rulebook, roster agents, generated skills and commands, and hook scripts), plus `settings.example.json` and `hooks.node.example.json` |
| `extras/worklog/`, `extras/peon/` | Optional Windows-only Claude Code hook scripts (run from the setup checkout; not installed into `~/.claude/tools/`) |

| Generated (do not edit) | Written by |
|---|---|
| `tests/golden/**` | `node tools/orc.mjs golden` |
| `dist/` (untracked) | `node tools/orc.mjs build` |

`node tools/orc.mjs check` compares every adapter's build with `tests/golden/<tool>/` and names the source to edit when a golden file is missing, differs or is stale. Rulebooks and Codex TOML agents carry a `generated by orc.mjs` marker on their first lines, and generated skills and commands on the first line after their front matter; Claude Code `agents/*.md` do not, to save tokens in every agent prompt. The marker is how `install` tells its own output from a hand copy.

## The edit loop

```
# 1. edit a source (a new or renamed skill or command: core/procedures.mjs plus the adapters' procedureNotes)
node tools/orc.mjs golden    # regenerates tests/golden/<tool>/
git diff tests/golden        # review: is every change one you meant?
npm test
node tools/orc.mjs check     # watch the antigravity headroom line
```

In Claude Code and Antigravity, the `ship-prompts` project skill walks this loop plus the README and wiki co-change and the live install.

`node tools/orc.mjs help` lists every command; `help <command>` lists its options. The full reference is `docs/cli.md`.

## Traps
- **A `~/.claude` checkout must not pull this layout.** The repo used to be checked out as `~/.claude`; `README.md` ("Moving off a `~/.claude` checkout") gives the exact seven-step migration order (clone elsewhere, configure `~/.orc/config.json`, delete the old tracked files `install` now owns, install from the clone, update hooks and timeline task, move logs and delete `~/.claude/.git` and `board.local.md`, run `doctor`).

- **`.gitignore`.** Standard deny-list: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `models.local.json`, `/board.local.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.env`, `.env.*`, `.orc/`, `orchestration/board/`, `orchestration/log/*` (except `TEMPLATE.md`), `.claude/*` (except `.claude/skills/ship-prompts/`), `.agents/*` (except `.agents/skills/ship-prompts/`) and editor/OS noise stay ignored so local state never gets staged.
- **Review tier.** Editing `core/AGENTS.md`, `core/roles/`, root `roles/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, `adapters/*.notes.md`, `adapters/<tool>/` (commands, skills), `profiles/`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`, any `SKILL.md`, `standards/`, `review/`, `workflows/`, `orchestration/{standards,sprint,board,brief,wrap-up}.md` or `orchestration/sprint/` makes `node tools/orc.mjs review-tier` say `Full`: prompts count as product, not docs.
- **The board is another repo.** The board page code (Co0pDawg/Orc-Dashboard) is its own repo, cloned wherever `board.repo` in `~/.orc/config.json` points (suggested: `~/.orc/board`). This machine's board address lives in `~/.orc/config.json` (`board.url`, and `board.repo` for a local board); `board.local.md` is retired: put its address in `~/.orc/config.json` `board.url` (with `board.repo` for a local board), delete any unrecorded hand-copied `~/.claude/tools/board-reminder.*` if `doctor` flags it, run `install --tool claude-code --apply` (or `sync --apply`), then delete `~/.claude/board.local.md`.
- **`extras/worklog`** is a Windows-only example with its own `extras/worklog/test.ps1`. Its tests assert US Eastern local times, so CI sets the runner to Eastern time first.
- **`models.local.json`** is untracked. `check` validates it, but builds and compares from `models.json` only; `golden` reads `models.json` only. `build`, `install`, `sync`, `status`, `dispatch` and `doctor` use it. `~/.orc/models.json` (or `$ORC_DATA_DIR/models.json`) layers between the two for `install`, `sync`, `status`, `dispatch` and `doctor` only; `build`, `check` and `golden` never read `~/.orc`.

## Adding or refreshing a standards entry

The archive in `standards/` feeds `node tools/orc.mjs standards apply`, which composes a project's `STANDARDS.md`.

- Follow the format in `standards/README.md`: the frontmatter fields, the section order, and a `## Review checklist` with `- [ ]` items.
- Cite primary sources only (language or vendor docs, official style guides, the linter's own docs). End every rule with `[n]`, the n-th URL in `sources`.
- Paraphrase: write every rule in your own words and never copy sentences from a source.
- No company, project or ticket names: the archive is public. A team's own rules go into its project through `apply --from`.
- When refreshing an entry, recheck its sources and update `reviewed`.
- Run `node tools/orc.mjs check`: it validates every entry (id matches the file name, kind, detect, requires, the reviewed date, citation range and the checklist). Then try `node tools/orc.mjs standards apply --repo <temp dir> --stack <id>`.

## Standalone checkout and the live install

This repo is a standalone checkout that installs into each tool's home folder; nothing checked in here is loaded as the product rulebook.

- Compare the live installs with the checkout: `node tools/orc.mjs status --all` (or `status --tool claude-code`). It writes nothing; it reports each file as `same`, `differs`, `missing`, `stale` or `extra`, and exits 0 only when all are `same`.
- Update every active tool listed in `~/.orc/config.json`: `node tools/orc.mjs sync` (dry run), then `node tools/orc.mjs sync --apply` (backs up every file it replaces). Or install one tool with `node tools/orc.mjs install --tool <id> [--home <dir>] --apply` (`--home` defaults to your home for every tool, `claude-code` included). Try a temp `--home` first when testing changes.
- Opening a session in this repo loads only the short contributor `AGENTS.md` (imported by root `CLAUDE.md`), never a second copy of `core/AGENTS.md`.

## Where things are

- `tools/orc.mjs`: the CLI. Loads roles, models and adapters, builds each tool (`buildTool`), and dispatches the commands.
- `tools/lib/`: `frontmatter.mjs` (frontmatter, generated marker), `roles.mjs` (role parsing), `models.mjs` (models validation), `toml.mjs` (Codex TOML), `manifest.mjs` (install manifest, path safety), `text.mjs` (the one text reader), `help.mjs` (the help table), `brief.mjs`, `reviewtier.mjs`, `prsize.mjs`, `textcheck.mjs`, `poll.mjs` (the commands the workflows run in place of shell snippets), `costlog.mjs`, `dispatch.mjs`, `hooks.mjs` (the method-tooling commands; also reads and writes `settings.json`), `sprintkit.mjs` (the sprint kit: presets, stack detection, the `settings.json` plan and removal), `standards.mjs` (the standards archive, detect and apply), `config.mjs` (the shared state home `~/.orc`: `config.json` validation, routing chains, the board default), `doctor.mjs` (`orc doctor`), `calibration.mjs`, `corpus.mjs` and `metrics.mjs` (the review panel's calibration, regression corpus and metrics), `bench.mjs` (`bench`: the replay benchmark) and `queue.mjs` (`queue`: the unattended issue queue).
- `tests/orc.test.mjs`: goldens, roles, frontmatter, caps (the skill body cap included), `check`, `install`, rulebook hygiene, the procedure catalogue and its generated wrappers, the one checkout lookup sentence, the scans for Claude Code only tools in Antigravity skills and the neutral procedures, and `uninstall --tool antigravity` with `orc-guard` in `hooks.json`.
- `tests/hardening.test.mjs`: option parsing, refusals, stale goldens, YAML quoting, running through a junction, BOM and UTF-16 input, first differing line.
- `tests/manifest.test.mjs`: install manifest, re-install, `uninstall`, `status`, symlink and junction refusals.
- `tests/sprintkit.test.mjs`: `install --sprint-kit` over real home shapes (none, populated, invalid, re-applied, a full install), the `settings.json` merge and restore, stack detection, presets, and the onboarding doc.
- `tests/tooling.test.mjs`: `brief`, `review-tier`, `costlog`, `dispatch` (with the Antigravity result object read for an honest exit code), `hooks`, the board reminder, models validation, `golden`, `help`, the generated marker.
- `tests/workflow-tools.test.mjs`: `pr-size` (against real git repos), `text-check`, `poll` (mostly through injected runs and clock; two real polls wait: one whose command is killed at a 1-second deadline, and a 2-second one of a helper that fails every run), and `now` (with injected UTC offsets): the commands the workflows run in place of shell snippets.
- `tests/config.test.mjs`: the shared state home (`config.json`, `~/.orc/models.json`), routed `dispatch`, `--prefer`, `--model`, `doctor`, `sync`, and `install --all` / `status --all`, with no real agent CLI on PATH.
- `tests/standards.test.mjs`: `standards list`, `show`, `detect` and `apply`, and the archive validation in `check`.
- `tests/guard.test.mjs`: the git guard, `tools/guard.mjs` and `tools/guard.ps1` through one table of PreToolUse payloads in real temporary repos (both hooks must give the same decision), the Antigravity payloads and `ORC_HEADLESS` and the `~` home lookup (`guard.mjs` only), the read-only role list against `core/roles/*.md`, fail-open lines, and the example-file wiring.
- `tests/review-tools.test.mjs`: `calibration`, `corpus` and `metrics`, over the run-log fixtures in `tests/fixtures/reviews/` and the corpus cases in `tests/fixtures/corpus/` (format: `review/corpus.md`).
- `tests/make-story.test.mjs`: `orchestration/sprint/make-story.mjs`: escaping, the event and meta checks, argument and I/O errors, BOM input, running through a junction.
- `tests/story-page.test.mjs`: the story template's inline script, run in `node:vm` against a stub document: sorting, kinds, clock times, tiles and the wrong-root alert.
- `tests/sprint-theme.test.mjs`: `orchestration/sprint/theme/theme.css`: tokens per look, WCAG contrast per look, reduced motion, no network loads, and the README head script's look list.
- `tests/theme-picker.test.mjs`: the picker's exported logic: the typed sequence, editable targets (including a shadow root), the brand press window and the initial look.
- `tests/helpers.mjs`: shared test helpers; every test file that imports `main` from `tools/orc.mjs` or spawns `tools/orc.mjs` must call `isolateHome()` after its imports (enforced by a meta-test in `tests/hardening.test.mjs`, with an explicit allow-list for home-independent files).
- `tests/bench.test.mjs`: `bench list`, `run` and `report` through a stub `claude`, over the replay cases in `tests/fixtures/bench/` (format: `orchestration/bench.md`).
- `tests/queue.test.mjs`: `queue list` and `run` through stub `gh` and `claude` executables and real git against a temp repo with a local bare origin: eligibility, outcomes, markers and retries, the lock, the push routes and the allow rules.

## Keep the README and wiki current

Every pull request that changes what a user sees or does updates the README and the wiki as part of the same change, not in a later docs pass. That covers a command, a flag, a role, a workflow, a skill, a mode, an install or restore step, a supported tool, or a limit that is added, changed or removed.

- **README.md** is in this repo, so its edit goes in the same commit range as the change.
- **The wiki** is its own repo, `https://github.com/Co0pDawg/Orc-istration.wiki.git`. Clone it, edit the matching page (the Home page index says which page covers what), add any new page to `_Sidebar.md` and the Home page index, and keep the `Next: [[...]]` chain unbroken. Push the wiki once the pull request merges, so the wiki never describes unmerged work.
- **The pull request description** carries a Docs line: the README sections and wiki pages updated, or `no user-facing change`. The pull request template asks for it.
- **Reviewers and refuters** treat a stale README section or wiki page as a must-fix, the same as a stale `docs/cli.md` entry.
- Evidence drawn from cost logs or other projects is anonymised before it goes in either place: the repo and the wiki are public.

## Pull requests

Branch off `main` and open a draft pull request against `main`. Fill in the template's Docs checklist (see "Keep the README and wiki current"). CI runs `npm test` and `node tools/orc.mjs check` on Ubuntu and Windows, plus the worklog test on Windows.
